source: Wright, Borbolla, Segall et al. (2019) Critical care information display approaches and design frameworks: systematic review and meta-analysis
finding: Review of 56 simulated-task display evaluations (32 critical care, 22 anesthesia displays). Making functional relationships visible (the EID idea, which needs a work domain analysis) was one of four design features tested against positive outcomes.
numbers: 56 manuscripts; searched 1990 to mid-2018. Of four design features compared by Fisher exact tests, only iterative evaluation with end users was significant (p<0.01).
limits: Binary positive/negative counting, not effect sizes. Simulated tasks only. EID alone was not significant in the text read. One author extracted, a second checked.
agent_relevance: A domain model alone did not predict success; testing the output with real users did. Pair an S0 gate with a check loop.

source: Wright, Borbolla, Segall et al. (2019) Critical care information display approaches and design frameworks: systematic review and meta-analysis (iterative evaluation)
finding: Displays designed with iterative evaluation with end users had a positive result in every study. Displays without it did far worse.
numbers: 14 of 14 positive with iterative evaluation vs 13 of 22 without. Two or more design processes: 17 of 20 positive vs 10 of 16 for one or none (p=0.15, not significant).
limits: Small counts, 90% binomial CIs. Confounded: well-resourced teams do both. Not an EID-only contrast.
agent_relevance: Revising the domain model against feedback matters more than stacking methods. Supports a revise-the-problem-model loop after S0.

source: Wright, Borbolla, Segall et al. (2019) Critical care information display approaches and design frameworks: systematic review and meta-analysis (clinical trials contrast)
finding: In a parallel review of real clinical trials, novel displays succeeded less often than in simulated tasks.
numbers: 9 of 17 displays positive (53%) in clinical trials vs 27 of 36 (75%) in the simulated experiments (14+13 positive of 14+22, derived from counts above).
limits: Different review for trials; publication bias likely in both.
agent_relevance: Lab gains from a domain-based design shrink in the field. Expect benchmark gains to shrink on real tasks.

source: Morice, Rakotomamonjy, Serres, Ruffier (2021) Ecological design of augmentation improves helicopter ship landing maneuvers (PLoS One)
finding: Novices landed a simulated helicopter on a ship. An augmentation built on the task's own perceptual variable (tau-dot kept near -0.5) shortened landing time and improved control. An augmentation that only fixed occlusion did less.
numbers: 16 participants (13 men, 3 women, mean age 24.7); within-subject: Calm vs Rough sea and Control, Replication, Addition. Cooper-Harper: Augmentation F(2,26)=4.87, p<0.05, partial eta2=0.27; Sea F(1,13)=105.62, p<0.001, eta2=0.89 (1.64 vs 4.55).
limits: Novices, fixed-base simulator, one task, n=16. The constraint came from perception research, not a formal abstraction hierarchy.
agent_relevance: Showing what the domain constrains beat showing what the user lacks. Model the job's constraints first, then help on the constraint that matters.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) Design and evaluation of ecological interface of driving warning system based on AR-HUD (Sensors 24)
finding: An AR-HUD warning interface built from an abstraction hierarchy and SRK analysis lowered workload and perception time versus a common interface in 3 of 5 scenarios.
numbers: 25 drivers aged 22-27. DALI total 21.45 vs 30.84 (eco vs common). S2: 18.91 vs 34.18, p<0.001; S3: 22.73 vs 32.18, p<0.01; S1 and S4 not significant (p=0.324, 0.391). Fixation 0.55 vs 0.69 s; pupil 4.75 vs 5.10 mm. Perception time 62.96% shorter in the full warning scenario.
limits: Young drivers only, simulator, two designs differing in many ways (position, form), so effect cannot be pinned on the analysis.
agent_relevance: Gains appear when the task is complex (multi-warning) and vanish when simple (S1). Use S0 to spend effort only on complex tasks.

source: Amelink (2010) Ecological automation design, extending work domain analysis (TU Delft thesis)
finding: Applied work domain analysis to aircraft energy display, autopilot and UAV design. Says the benefit could not be measured cleanly because the creative design step after the analysis drives success.
numbers: Pilot evaluation was preliminary and subjective: pilots first found the display complex, later comments very positive. Author expected performance may stay unchanged while the way of working changes.
quote: An evaluation of how the approach limits complexity has not been found feasible
limits: No controlled test of WDA vs no WDA. A rival display from a different analysis (Catton et al. 2007) would give different results, so analysis cannot be separated from design skill.
agent_relevance: Credit-assignment problem: the model and the later step are fused. Do not expect a clean ablation of S0 alone.

source: Amelink (2010) (analyst reliability and effort)
finding: The abstraction hierarchy lacks rules for which fact goes on which level, and for validating and revising the model. Closed-loop control cannot be shown across levels. Building it took a significant amount of time.
numbers: No numbers; cites Vicente (2002) and Lind (2003) for the lack of guidelines. Benefit noted: the analyst became very familiar with the domain.
limits: Qualitative author judgement from own design cases (aircraft, UAV, sailing).
agent_relevance: Method is analyst-dependent, so an LLM doing it is not obviously worse than a human. Output needs checking; no accepted validation exists.

source: Boyce, Sottilare, Goldberg, Amburn (2015) Work domain analysis for ecological interface design of tangible interfaces (I/ITSEC)
finding: A WDA for a military augmented-reality sandtable was built from technical documents, prior research and a few subject matter experts. Interface evaluation was left as future work.
numbers: No user data. Authors plan future usability experiments and a tutor.
limits: Expert-validated only; no experiment.
agent_relevance: Most applied WDA papers stop at the model. Do not cite them as evidence of benefit.

source: Upton and Doherty (2008) Visual representation of complex information structures in high volume manufacturing
finding: Used the abstraction hierarchy and EID guidance to design visual tools for semiconductor manufacturing.
numbers: No controlled performance comparison found in the text read.
limits: Design case, not a test.
agent_relevance: Same pattern: method adoption is wide, hard evidence is thin.

source: Wikipedia (read 2026) Ecological interface design
finding: EID arose from Risoe work by Vicente and Rasmussen in the late 1980s; aim is to make work-domain constraints perceptible so users can reason at the knowledge-based level, including for unanticipated events.
numbers: No effect sizes on the page.
limits: Secondary source, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Rationale for the gate: handle novel problems by modelling constraints, not by recalling procedures.

source: Elite netball organisation cognitive work analysis (2019, Frontiers) Sports organizations as complex systems
finding: Work domain analysis plus social organisation analysis of an elite netball organisation from one expert workshop.
numbers: 13 subject matter experts (5 male, 8 female, age M=43.9, SD=14.3), one workshop, five researchers. No outcome measure.
limits: Single organisation, model not validated against performance, expert opinion only.
agent_relevance: Domain models come from a few experts in one session; coverage and bias are untested.

source: ICU nurse patient-mobility work domain analysis (2022)
finding: Abstraction hierarchy built to find constraints on ICU nurses' mobility decisions, to guide decision support.
numbers: 32 hours of observation and interviews with 20 nurses at 2 hospitals.
limits: Descriptive; no intervention tested.
agent_relevance: Shows the data volume a human WDA needs. An LLM gate should say when it lacks such data.

source: Payyanadan and Lee (2021) Representing route familiarity using the abstraction hierarchy framework
finding: Free-text driver feedback was mapped onto abstraction hierarchy levels.
numbers: 32 drivers aged 65+, 3 months of OBDII logging with trip diaries.
limits: Coding to levels is analyst judgement; no inter-rater figure seen.
agent_relevance: Mapping free text to levels is what an LLM can do; test reliability against human coders.

source: Modeling automation with cognitive work analysis to support human-automation coordination (2017, trading)
finding: CWA of financial trading with automation. Direct observation of professional traders was impossible because of confidentiality, so staff traders were consulted on missing function allocations.
numbers: No quantitative evaluation.
limits: Access limits cap model completeness.
agent_relevance: Gate should record which parts of the domain model are assumed, not observed.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Abstraction hierarchy to define biofoundry workflows (Nature Communications)
finding: Proposed four levels (Project, Service/Capability, Workflow, Unit Operation) to standardise biofoundry work; claims modular, automated workflows.
numbers: No controlled outcome numbers in the abstract.
limits: Proposal paper; benefit claimed, not measured.
agent_relevance: Abstraction levels as a schema for decomposing a job into machine-runnable units. Useful pattern, unproven.

source: Workload management scoping review in nuclear control rooms (2025)
finding: In Rasmussen's home domain, tested evidence on operator workload support is still scarce.
numbers: 49 studies: 40 on technical systems or interfaces, 11 on procedures, 3 on training. Only 11 evaluated workload empirically.
limits: Scoping review, no effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Hard evidence is thin even in the core domain.

source: ACTIVE meta-methodology (2026, MethodsX) action-oriented method for complex or chaotic problems
finding: Proposes classifying how disordered a problem is (Cynefin) before choosing a strategy: experiment first when causes only show through intervention.
numbers: No empirical test.
limits: Untested framework.
agent_relevance: A rival S0 gate: classify by predictability, not by job structure. Needs a head-to-head.

source: Vicente and Rasmussen (1990, 1992)
finding: A search snippet quotes the authors: initial empirical evaluation gave only preliminary support for EID.
numbers: None read.
limits: Snippet only; not opened.
agent_relevance: Original support is weak; later work is mostly in simulators.

source: Flexible manufacturing system CSE/EID study (SAGE 10.1177/15553434221118978, seen in a search snippet)
finding: Snippet says the ecological interface gave 32 favourable significant results against 28 for the other three interfaces combined; an earlier test had 10 of 11 significant effects favouring it.
numbers: 32 vs 28 significant results; 10 of 11 earlier.
limits: Snippet only; counts significant tests, not effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Counting significant tests inflates; treat as weak support.

source: Pawlak and Vicente (1996) DURESS II EID experiment (named in Amelink thesis)
finding: Classic EID test on the DURESS II process simulator; Amelink cites DURESS II as an abstraction-hierarchy example.
numbers: Numbers not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Open next for exact effect sizes.

source: Jungk et al. (1999, 2000) ecological displays for hemodynamic monitoring and anesthesia (listed in the 2019 review reference list)
finding: Two ecological display approaches for the anesthesia workplace were evaluated against conventional ones.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Only the reference list was seen.
agent_relevance: Open next for numbers.

source: Militello, Dominguez, Lintern, Klein (2009) (cited in Amelink thesis)
finding: Cited by Amelink as agreeing that the work domain model acts as an integrating thread through design, not a one-off phase.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports keeping S0's model alive through later states.

source: Search coverage note (this agent)
finding: No LLM study using work domain analysis, abstraction hierarchy or CWA as an agent or prompting method was found. The web search budget was used up and arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar all returned 429 limits. One Europe PMC query with LLM terms gave 5 hits, none relevant except the ACTIVE paper.
numbers: 0 LLM studies found.
limits: Absence from a blocked search, not proof none exist.
agent_relevance: Treat LLM tests of S0-style job mapping as an open gap; rerun the arXiv search later.

source: Cross-source pattern (this agent)
finding: Across the sources read, gains from domain-constraint design show in complex or novel cases and in simulators; no controlled test separates the analysis from design skill; method authors admit the analysis depends on the analyst.
numbers: 14/14 vs 13/22 (iterative evaluation); 17/20 vs 10/16 (p=0.15); 9/17 in clinical trials.
limits: Synthesis of a small, non-random set.
agent_relevance: Use S0 as a cheap routing step with a feedback loop; expect small, task-dependent gains.
